info.name: VoltStore API (through the gateway)
info.description:
Every request goes through the API Gateway, the single entry point. Run the whole collection with the Collection Runner (or newman) from top to bottom: each request saves what the next ones need (tokens, ids), and checks its status and body.

**Before running**, set the collection variables:
- `baseUrl`: `http://localhost:8080` for Docker Compose; `http://127.0.0.1/api` for Kubernetes through the Ingress (`minikube tunnel`).
- `adminPassword`: the admin password of the running stack (`AUTH_ADMIN_PASSWORD` in `auth-service/.env`, or the auth secret in Kubernetes). It is empty in the file on purpose.

Every run registers new accounts and a new product (names end with a run id), so it can be repeated on the same database.

**Waiting:** steps that depend on Kafka events repeat themselves (1 s apart, up to 20 times) until the event has arrived. Login and register are rate-limited to 5 calls per minute, so a run waits out the 429 once or twice (Retry-After) and takes about 2–3 minutes. Polling and waiting work only in the Runner; a single "Send" shows the current state.

exec: // Wait before a repeated request: a poll for a Kafka event, or a retry after a 429
// Rate limit (5 logins/registrations per minute): wait for Retry-After and repeat the request

item.name: 0. Setup
item.description: Creates run-unique names so the collection can be run again and again on the same database.

request.description: Any public call; its pre-request script prepares the variables of this run (unique e-mails and names).

exec: if (!pm.collectionVariables.get('adminPassword')) { throw new Error('Set the collection variable adminPassword (AUTH_ADMIN_PASSWORD of auth-service/.env, or the k8s auth secret)'); }

item.name: 1. Auth — registration and login
item.description: Demo scenario: registration and login. Auth Service issues the JWT; the gateway verifies it on every other call.

request.description: EP-AUTH: public. Creates a CUSTOMER account.
Bean Validation on the record DTO; the ProblemDetail lists the invalid fields.

item.name: Log in with a wrong password → 401

request.description: The admin account is seeded by Auth Service from AUTH_ADMIN_EMAIL / AUTH_ADMIN_PASSWORD.
The gateway checks the role from the JWT before the request reaches Auth Service.

item.name: Log in as the catalog manager
Log in as the inventory worker
2. Catalog — categories and products (manager)
item.description: Catalog Service owns categories and products. A new product is published to Kafka (catalog.product-events), and Inventory creates its stock item from that event.

item.name: Create a category without a token → 401

request.description: New products start NOT_ACTIVE. Saving the product and its ProductCreated event happen in one transaction (transactional outbox).

item.name: Create a product with invalid data → 400
3. Inventory — stock and packaging (worker)
item.description: Inventory Service owns stock. The stock item appears asynchronously, from the ProductCreated event; the first request polls until it exists.

item.name: Stock item created from the Kafka event

exec: const ready = (() => { try { return pm.response.code === 200; } catch (e) { return false; } })();

request.description: Delivery needs the parcel size to register a shipment, so a product cannot be activated without packaging.

item.name: 4. Activation and storefront
item.description: Activating calls Inventory synchronously (REST, @HttpExchange) to check the packaging. The storefront stock status comes back from Inventory through Kafka (inventory.stock-events).

request.description: Answers 200 with no body; the next request shows the product ACTIVE in the storefront.

item.name: Product in the storefront is IN_STOCK

exec: const ready = (() => { try { return pm.response.json().stockStatus === 'IN_STOCK'; } catch (e) { return false; } })();

item.name: 5. Customer — profile and cart
item.description: Customer Service owns the profile and the server-side cart.

item.name: Add the product to the cart

exec: pm.test('one line, quantity 2', () => { const line = pm.response.json().find(i => i.productId === pm.collectionVariables.get('productId')); pm.expect(line.quantity).to.eql(2); });

item.name: 6. Business scenario 1 — place, pay and ship an order
item.description:
The checkout saga, orchestrated by Order Service:
1. Place: Order reads prices from Catalog (REST) and reserves stock in Inventory (gRPC).
2. Pay: Order charges the card through Payment (REST). OrderPaid goes to Kafka: Customer clears the cart, Delivery registers the parcel and reports the TTN.
3. Ship: the worker ships the order; OrderShipped makes Inventory deduct the reserved stock.
Test cards of the mock payment gateway: ending 4242 approved, 0002 insufficient funds, any other declined.

item.name: Check the cart can be ordered

request.description: An order line is limited to 10 units.

item.name: Repeat with the same Idempotency-Key → same order

request.description: A retried submit (for example after a timeout) does not create a second order.

item.name: Pay with a card without funds → 402
Cart cleared by the OrderPaid event

exec: const ready = (() => { try { return pm.response.json().length === 0; } catch (e) { return false; } })();
const ready = (() => { try { return pm.response.json().deliveryStatus === 'TTN_GENERATED'; } catch (e) { return false; } })();

item.name: Stock deducted by the OrderShipped event

exec: const ready = (() => { try { return pm.response.json().totalQuantity === 8; } catch (e) { return false; } })();

item.name: 7. Business scenario 2 — cancel a paid order (refund)
item.description: Cancelling a paid order runs the cancellation saga: Order refunds the payment (Payment, REST), cancels the shipment (Delivery, REST) and releases the reservation (Inventory, gRPC).

exec: const ready = (() => { try { return pm.response.json().status === 'CANCELLED'; } catch (e) { return false; } })();

item.name: 8. Business scenario 3 — cancel before payment
item.description: An unpaid order is cancelled at once and its reservation released; no payment is touched. Orders not paid in time expire the same way (PaymentWindowExpiryJob).

item.name: Ordering more than is in stock → 422

request.description: Only 8 are left; Order asks Inventory and lists the line as INSUFFICIENT_STOCK.

item.name: 9. Gateway protection
item.description: The API Gateway is the single entry point: it verifies the JWT, checks the role and limits the request rate.

item.name: Rate limit: 6th login within a minute → 429

request.description: Login and register are limited to 5 calls per minute per client IP. This request repeats itself until the gateway answers 429. Run it last: logins are blocked for up to a minute afterwards.
